title: release-readiness.yml
description: Validates the repository-root release-readiness.yml. Enforced by scripts/validate-manifests.py in `make check`, which additionally rejects a `passed` result whose revision_tested is not the current HEAD. This file is the traceability spine: every success test the pack claims, what implements it, what checks it, who owns it, which revision was tested, and the current result. It also holds the canonical document id list that sources.yml and claims-ledger.json are cross-checked against.

release_status.description: Two labels, never blurred. PREVIEW is honestly incomplete: workspace or admin rows may be not-run provided the missing authority and next action are explicit. RELEASE-READY means all four success tests passed against this candidate, with the human validations performed by representative users rather than by the authoring agent.

result_definitions.description: Defined in the file itself so no reader has to infer what not-run means. not-run is not a soft pass.

standalone.description: True for documents that must be useful when forwarded alone, with no repository access. Success test 4 depends on at least one.

closed_by.description: Who can honestly close it. A test about what a person experiences cannot be closed by the builder; recording that in machine-readable form is what stops the claim drifting into the README.

artifact.description: What in the repository implements it.

automated_checks.description: CI job or make target names. May be empty for a test no machine can check, which is itself worth seeing.

human_validation.description: The validation protocol that closes it, or null when none is needed. A humans-closed test with null here is a contradiction and the validator says so.

revision_tested.description: Full SHA the recorded result was produced against, or `none` when it has not been run. A short SHA is rejected: it is ambiguous across a repository's lifetime.

verified_by.description: Who or what produced the recorded result.

then.description: A passed result names its evidence, the revision it passed against, and who ran it. Without all three, `passed` is an opinion.
A not-run or failed row must say what is missing and what the next action is, so a PREVIEW handover is legible rather than merely incomplete.
If people close it, the protocol they follow has to exist and be named.
